chunks: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-'Abbas, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Hariz, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man sees something in sleep and feels desire, then he wakes up and looks but does not see anything; then after a short while it comes out. He said: If he is ill, then let him perform ghusl, and if he is not ill, then there is nothing upon him. He said: I said to him: So what is the difference between the two? He said: Because when a man is healthy, the fluid comes with a strong gush, but if he is ill, it does not come except afterward.

key_terms.الشَّهْوَةَ: sexual desire or arousal felt during the dream
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: the seminal fluid referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep; the state in which the dream is seen
key_terms.صَحِيحًا: healthy; one whose discharge normally comes forcefully
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no obligation upon him
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: ill; a condition that affects how the fluid exits

ai.seo_question: Does delayed discharge after sleep require ghusl if no fluid is seen immediately upon waking?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about ghusl in the case of seeing an erotic dream and delayed discharge. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام distinguishes between a healthy person and an ill person, explaining that illness can delay the emergence of the fluid, which affects the ruling.
